hints: Notice the question distinguishes three energy terms: total energy input, useful energy output and wasted energy output.
Recall that efficiency measures what fraction of the supplied energy is converted to the desired useful form, so useful output must be on top.
Compare each fraction: check which one has useful output divided by total input and which ones invert it, add wasted energy, or use wasted energy alone.
walkthrough: Identify the given terms: the system is supplied with total energy input and produces useful energy output plus wasted energy output.
State the physical rule: efficiency = $\frac{\text{useful output}}{\text{total input}}$, where both quantities can be energy or power in the same units.
Check conservation: total energy input = useful energy output + wasted energy output, so efficiency is always less than 1.
Test option A: $\frac{\text{total input}}{\text{useful output}}$ is the reciprocal and exceeds 1, so it cannot be efficiency.
Test options B and D: B gives $\frac{\text{useful + wasted}}{\text{total input}} = 1$ and D gives the wasted fraction, neither is the useful fraction.
Therefore only $\frac{\text{useful energy output}}{\text{total energy input}}$ fits the definition. This is option C

options.A: This inverts the ratio as $\frac{\text{input}}{\text{useful output}}$, which would give a value greater than 1 for a real system.
options.B: The numerator $\text{useful output + wasted output}$ equals the total output, so this ratio is 1 by conservation of energy and does not measure usefulness.
options.C: Efficiency is defined as $\frac{\text{useful energy output}}{\text{total energy input}}$, which is always less than 1 for a real system.
options.D: This is $\frac{\text{wasted output}}{\text{total input}}$, which gives the fraction wasted, not the efficiency.
